nodes.label: Biolord’s learned latent representation is biologically informative; it reveals drug organization according to known corresponding pathways, and better captures
nodes.text: Biolord’s learned latent representation is biologically informative; it reveals drug organization according to known corresponding pathways, and better captures underlying drug organization, relative to the chemically informed RDKit features used as input, both qualitatively and quantitatively (adjusted Rand index RDKit: 0.03, biolord: 0.16; Supplementary Fig. 4). To further evaluate the quality of biolord’s drugs representation, we employ the uncertainty measure suggested by ref. 5, assessing the ability to predict the drug’s pathway from the k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) graph of the embedding space (Methods). Compared to RDKit, biolord’s uncertainty measure is found to be lower on average and more concentrated (distribution evaluated over all drugs; RDKit: 0.32±0.008, biolord: 0.19±0.005; Supplementary Fig. 4).

nodes.label: Biolord | Deep generative framework with decomposed latent space: each known attribute (categorical or ordered) has a dedicated subnetwork (embeddings for categ
nodes.text: Biolord | Deep generative framework with decomposed latent space: each known attribute (categorical or ordered) has a dedicated subnetwork (embeddings for categorical, MLP encoder for ordered), unknown attributes use per-sample embedding with Gaussian noise and L2 regularization. Generator (decoder) outputs distribution parameters (Gaussian, ZINB, or Poisson) from concatenated latent codes. Trained with completeness loss (negative log-likelihood + MSE) and minimality loss (L2 penalty on unknown embedding). Hyperparameters tuned via Weights & Biases.

attributes.protocol: Deep generative framework with decomposed latent space: each known attribute (categorical or ordered) has a dedicated subnetwork (embeddings for categorical, MLP encoder for ordered), unknown attributes use per-sample embedding with Gaussian noise and L2 regularization. Generator (decoder) outputs distribution parameters (Gaussian, ZINB, or Poisson) from concatenated latent codes. Trained with completeness loss (negative log-likelihood + MSE) and minimality loss (L2 penalty on unknown embedding). Hyperparameters tuned via Weights & Biases.

nodes.text: Figure 6 illustrates the ability of AttentionPert to capture the nonadditive nature of multiplexed genetic perturbations. When predicting a seen 2/2 perturbation: FOXA1 and HOXB9, AttentionPert is adept at learning the combined response of these genes. This approach differs markedly from a simple additive model, which merely sums the transcriptional effects of each gene perturbed independently.

nodes.label: AttentionPert | AttentionPert takes perturbation indicators as input into two modules: PertWeight and PertLocal encoders. Each outputs an encoding matrix (RK×D)
nodes.text: AttentionPert | AttentionPert takes perturbation indicators as input into two modules: PertWeight and PertLocal encoders. Each outputs an encoding matrix (RK×D). The sum is fed into a gene-specific linear decoder to predict the expression shift. The prediction is added to a random control sample. Loss function combines auto-focus and direction-aware loss (GEARS). Hyperparameters: embedding size De=200 (Gene2Vec), SGConv hops t=1, hidden size D=64, attention heads H=2, head dimension dq=dk=dv=64, GO graph edge weight multiplier α=0.75, NA-bias β=0.05, trained for 20 epochs, batch size 128, Adam optimizer with learning rate 1e-3.

attributes.protocol: AttentionPert takes perturbation indicators as input into two modules: PertWeight and PertLocal encoders. Each outputs an encoding matrix (RK×D). The sum is fed into a gene-specific linear decoder to predict the expression shift. The prediction is added to a random control sample. Loss function combines auto-focus and direction-aware loss (GEARS). Hyperparameters: embedding size De=200 (Gene2Vec), SGConv hops t=1, hidden size D=64, attention heads H=2, head dimension dq=dk=dv=64, GO graph edge weight multiplier α=0.75, NA-bias β=0.05, trained for 20 epochs, batch size 128, Adam optimizer with learning rate 1e-3.

nodes.text: xTrimoGene architecture | Scalable transformer-based model with embedding module and asymmetric encoder-decoder structure. nodes.label: RDA pretraining task | For each cell, a hierarchical Bayesian downsampling strategy generates a low total counts variant. Normalize and log-transform both raw a
nodes.text: RDA pretraining task | For each cell, a hierarchical Bayesian downsampling strategy generates a low total counts variant. Normalize and log-transform both raw and input vectors. Define T (target total counts of raw sample) and S (source total counts of input sample). Randomly mask 30% of both zero and nonzero genes. Model predicts raw expression at masked positions using masked input plus T and S indicators. Loss is regression (MSE) on masked positions.

nodes.text: MIMOSCA computational framework | A regularized linear model (elastic net) predicting each gene's expression as a function of guide effects, technical covariates (number of transcripts, detection probability), and biological covariates (cell state, subtype). nodes.text: Cell state definition | Cell states defined from unperturbed cells by selecting variable genes via Loess regression on coefficient of variation vs. mean expression, normalizing to 10,000 transcripts, log2 transformation, Z-transformation, randomized PCA retaining top ~10 components, clustering with Infomap, and iterative merging until no pairwise clusters have <100 differentially expressed genes (Welch's t test, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR).

attributes.protocol: Cell states defined from unperturbed cells by selecting variable genes via Loess regression on coefficient of variation vs. mean expression, normalizing to 10,000 transcripts, log2 transformation, Z-transformation, randomized PCA retaining top ~10 components, clustering with Infomap, and iterative merging until no pairwise clusters have <100 differentially expressed genes (Welch's t test, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR).

nodes.label: Here we propose a third and complementary screening paradigm, single-cell CRISPR screens, based on the idea that gRNAs and their induced cellular responses are
nodes.text: Here we propose a third and complementary screening paradigm, single-cell CRISPR screens, based on the idea that gRNAs and their induced cellular responses are already compartmentalized within single cells. Detecting each cell’s gRNA along with its single-cell transcriptome would thus provide gene expression signatures for individual gene knockouts in a complex pool of cells. Implementing this concept, our CROP-seq method combines four key components: a gRNA vector that makes individual gRNAs detectable in single-cell RNA-seq experiments, a high-throughput assay for single-cell RNA-seq7, a computational pipeline for assigning single-cell transcriptomes to gRNAs, and a bioinformatic method for analyzing and interpreting gRNA-induced transcriptional profiles.

The map Tk is then applied to unseen control cells to predict perturbed states.

Transfer learning is performed by pretraining on L1000 bulk RNA data and fine-tuning on sci-Plex3 single-cell data, handling differing gene sets via a projection layer or shared gene subset.
